chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I said to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: A man is in an open barren land on a cloudy day, so he performs salat (prayer) facing other than the qiblah, then the sky clears and he comes to know that he had performed salat (prayer) facing other than the qiblah. What should he do? He said: If he is still within the time, then let him repeat his salat (prayer); but if the time has passed, then his ijtihad is sufficient for him.

key_terms.اجْتِهَادُهُ: his reasoned effort to determine the qiblah under uncertain circumstances
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the direction one must face in salat (prayer)
key_terms.صَلَاتَهُ: his salat (prayer), which must be repeated if time remains
key_terms.غَيْمٍ: cloud cover that obscures guidance and contributes to uncertainty
key_terms.قَفْرٍ: a barren or desolate land where signs for determining direction may be absent

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone prayed in the wrong direction and later realized he had faced other than the qiblah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who performs salat (prayer) in the wrong direction due to uncertainty about the qiblah. If he discovers the mistake within the prayer time, he must repeat the salat (prayer); if he discovers it after the time has passed, his prior ijtihad suffices.
